title: What to Watch This Week: The Dragons Are Back, Pandora Comes Home, and a Jail Full of Celebrities Opens for Business
excerpt: From House of the Dragon's bloodiest season yet to Avatar: Fire and Ash landing in Hindi, here are the eight titles worth your weekend — and where the diaspora can stream them.
body:
It is the last full week of June, and your watchlist is about to buckle. JioHotstar and Netflix are each dropping four titles, the multiplexes are throwing a comedy carnival at you, and somewhere in a fake underground bunker, sixteen Indian celebrities are learning that loyalty is overrated. This is the kind of week where the hardest decision isn't *what* to watch — it's what to watch *first*.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=0JlMjgqduVw

So we did the sorting for you. Here are the eight that actually deserve your evenings, with where-to-stream sorted for the folks watching from Jersey City, Wembley and Brampton.

The Big One: House of the Dragon Season 3

JioHotstar | Streaming now

The Targaryens have stopped negotiating. After two seasons of simmering, the civil war finally catches fire — and Season 3 opens, ruthlessly, with a death. The Battle of the Gullet is the kind of set piece HBO has been quietly bankrupting itself to build: dragons over open water, fleets in flames, and Emma D'Arcy's Rhaenyra hardening into something colder than grief. Matt Smith remains the most watchable man in Westeros. If you have JioHotstar, clear your Sunday. This is appointment television, and the diaspora gets it day-and-date with the US — no more dodging spoilers from cousins back home.

Pandora Comes Home: Avatar: Fire and Ash

JioHotstar | Streaming now

![Jersey City — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Journal_Square_Jersey_City_November_2021_003.jpg/3840px-Journal_Square_Jersey_City_November_2021_003.jpg)

> "Essential viewing for anyone who still shouts "Jai Mahishmati" at parties."

James Cameron's third trip to Pandora made its theatrical fortune; now it lands on streaming dubbed in Hindi, Tamil and Telugu — which is precisely how a huge chunk of Indian households will finally meet the Sully family. On a good TV with the volume up, the bioluminescent reefs and the new fire-clan Na'vi look genuinely staggering. It is three-plus hours of pure spectacle. Put the phone down and let it swallow you.

The Quiet Heartbreaker: Gram Chikitsalay Season 2

Prime Video | Streaming now

TVF does it again. The little rural clinic at Bhathkandi is back, and Amol Parashar's Dr. Prabhat is still trying to fix a village that doesn't entirely want fixing. If you grew up on *Panchayat* and *Gullak*, this is your comfort food — gentle, funny, and sneakily moving. The warmest show on this list, and the easiest one to fall in love with.

The Chaos Pick: Alliance

Prime Video | June 26

Kunal Kemmu trades the camera for the host's mic in Prime Video's most ruthless reality experiment yet: sixteen celebrities, one underground bunker, and a game built entirely on betrayal. Think *The Traitors* with desi star wattage and zero chill. Reality TV is having a moment in India, and this one looks engineered to break group chats. Messy, addictive, exactly what a Tuesday needs.

The Theatrical Event: Welcome To The Jungle

In cinemas June 26 (paid previews June 25)

![Dragon Season — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9a/Busta_rhymes-06-mika.jpg)

Nineteen years after the original became a cult classic, Akshay Kumar marches back into the *Welcome* universe with what may be the most overstuffed ensemble in recent Bollywood memory — Suniel Shetty, Paresh Rawal, Arshad Warsi, Jacqueline Fernandez, Disha Patani, and a 22-years-later Raveena Tandon reunion that had the set on its feet. It won't reinvent comedy, but it isn't trying to. For NRI families, this is the Friday cinema outing — find your nearest desi-friendly multiplex and go loud.

The Wildcard: Supergirl

In cinemas June 26

Milly Alcock (yes, the young Rhaenyra) takes flight as Kara in James Gunn's expanding DCU, in a story that swaps cape-and-smile heroics for a darker revenge arc across the galaxy. The press tour already gave us the image of the week — co-star David Corenswet shielding Alcock from a falling photographer at the premiere — but the film itself promises real teeth. A worthy double-bill if you're already at the multiplex for Akshay.

The Sleeper: Blast

Netflix | June 25

The Tamil action-drama that quietly over-performed in theatres lands on Netflix — a middle-class family of fighters squaring off against a mining billionaire. Arjun Sarja anchors it. Grounded, scrappy, and a reminder that South Indian cinema keeps finding the muscle Bollywood sometimes forgets it has.

For the Superfans: Baahubali — The Torchbearer

Netflix | June 26

With SS Rajamouli's *Baahubali: The Eternal War* heading to Annecy, Netflix drops a documentary series cracking open the making of Maahishmati — the obsession, the scale, the near-bankrupting madness of it all. Essential viewing for anyone who still shouts "Jai Mahishmati" at parties.

The Verdict

If you watch one thing: *House of the Dragon*. If you want to switch your brain off: *Welcome To The Jungle*. If you want to feel something: *Gram Chikitsalay*. And if you just want to watch famous people stab each other in the back — *Alliance* opens the bunker Friday. See you on the other side of the binge.
